plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under the Companies Act, 2013, what is the timeline within which a foreign company must deliver documents to the Registrar of Companies (RoC) upon establishing a place of business in India?
options: 15 days
30 days
60 days
90 days
plain.explanation: Section 380 of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates that every foreign company shall, within 30 days of the establishment of place of business in India, deliver specified documents to the Registrar. This is a crucial procedural requirement for foreign entities operating in India.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following documents is NOT statutorily required to be delivered by a foreign company to the RoC under Section 380 upon establishing a place of business in India?
options: Certified copy of the charter, statutes or memorandum and articles of the company
Full address of the registered or principal office of the company
List of all past and present directors and secretary of the company
Audited balance sheet and profit and loss account for the preceding three financial years
plain.explanation: Section 380 requires filing of the charter, full address, list of directors, and details of principal place of business in India, among others. Audited financial statements of the Indian business are required to be filed annually under Section 381, but initial incorporation filings under Section 380 do not require three years of audited accounts.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: If any alteration is made or occurs in any of the documents delivered to the RoC by a foreign company under Section 380, within what period must the foreign company file a return containing particulars of such alteration?
options: 15 days
30 days
60 days
90 days
plain.explanation: According to Section 380(3), if any alteration is made or occurs in the documents delivered to the Registrar, the foreign company must file a return containing the particulars of the alteration within 30 days of such alteration.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Every foreign company is required to prepare and file financial statements relating to its Indian business operations with the RoC in Form:
options: FC-1
FC-3
AOC-4
MGT-7
plain.explanation: Under Rule 4 of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014, every foreign company must file balance sheet and profit and loss account in Form FC-3 along with a list of all places of business established by the company in India.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Within what period from the close of the financial year must a foreign company file its financial statements and list of places of business in India with the RoC?
options: 30 days
6 months
180 days
90 days
plain.explanation: As per Rule 4(1) of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014, every foreign company shall file with the Registrar, along with the financial statements, a list of all places of business established by the company in India within 6 months of the close of the financial year.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Who is empowered by the Central Government to direct that any foreign company or class of foreign companies shall comply with specific provisions regarding accounts and audit?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Central Government by notification
National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)
plain.explanation: Section 381(3) states that the Central Government may, by notification, direct that the provisions of Chapter IX (Accounts of Companies) or any specified provisions thereof shall apply to any foreign company or class of foreign companies with such exceptions or modifications as may be specified.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Where a foreign company keeps its books of account outside India, what is the statutory requirement regarding copies of such books of account to be kept at its principal place of business in India?
options: No books need to be kept in India
Periodic returns reflecting the financial position of business in India must be kept at the principal place of business
Complete original ledger books must be shipped to India monthly
Certified translated copies of all global accounts must be maintained in India
plain.explanation: Section 381(1) proviso requires that a foreign company must keep at its principal place of business in India books of account containing sufficient particulars to show the true and fair view of the transactions of the company and explain its receipts and payments, as well as periodic returns reflecting the financial position of the business in India.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 382, every foreign company must paint or affix its name and the name of the country in which it is incorporated outside every office or place of business in India in:
options: English language only
Official language of the state where the office is located
English and local language of the place where its office is situated
Hindi only
plain.explanation: Section 382 requires every foreign company to exhibit its name and the country of incorporation in English and in the local language of the place where its office or place of business is situated, outside every office or place of business in India.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the penalty under Section 392 for a foreign company that fails to comply with any of the provisions of Chapter XXII (Companies Incorporated Outside India)?
options: Fine ranging from ₹10,000 to ₹1,00,000 only
Fine not less than ₹1,00,000 which may extend to ₹3,00,000, and in case of continuing offence with a further fine up to ₹50,000 per day
Imprisonment of directors only
Automatic winding up of the foreign company
plain.explanation: Section 392 prescribes a fine for the company not less than ₹1,00,000 extending up to ₹3,00,000, and in case of continuing offence, an additional fine up to ₹50,000 per day for every officer in default or the company. This ensures strict compliance.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following defines a 'foreign company' under Section 2(42) of the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Any company incorporated outside India which has a share capital
Any company or body corporate incorporated outside India which has a place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent, physically or through electronic mode
Any company owned by non-resident Indians operating outside India
Any multinational corporation trading with Indian entities without any physical office
plain.explanation: Section 2(42) defines a foreign company as any company or body corporate incorporated outside India which has a place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent, physically or through electronic mode, and conducts any business activity in India in any other manner.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Can a foreign company issue prospectus in India without complying with Chapter XXII provisions?
options: Yes, if it is listed on a recognized foreign stock exchange
No, it must comply with all statutory prospectus provisions under Sections 389 to 393
Yes, if approved by SEBI independently
No, foreign companies are completely barred from issuing prospectuses in India
plain.explanation: Sections 389 to 393 govern the issue of prospectus by foreign companies. No prospectus can be issued by or on behalf of a foreign company unless it complies with the stringent disclosure and delivery requirements specified in the Act.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: When a prospectus is issued by a foreign company in India, a copy thereof must be delivered to:
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Registrar of Companies at Delhi
Reserve Bank of India
Ministry of Corporate Affairs directly
plain.explanation: Section 389 stipulates that no person shall issue, circulate or distribute in India any prospectus offering for subscription shares or debentures of a company incorporated outside India, unless a copy has been delivered to the Registrar of Companies (specifically designated RoC, typically Delhi).

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which rule defines 'electronic mode' for the purpose of a foreign company conducting business in India?
options: Rule 2 of Companies (Specification of Definitions Details) Rules, 2014
Rule 3 of Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014
Rule 5 of Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014
Rule 10 of Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014
plain.explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014 defines 'electronic mode' encompassing business-to-business and business-to-consumer transactions, data interchange, online services, digital supply chains, etc., conducted via electronic media.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What must be stated prominently on the outside of every office and in all business letters, bill heads, and notices of a foreign company in India?
options: The PAN and GSTIN of the Indian branch
Whether the company is limited or not, along with its name and country of incorporation
The name of the Chief Executive Officer of the Indian operations
The authorized share capital in Indian Rupees
plain.explanation: Under Section 382, foreign companies must state the name of the company, the country of incorporation, and if the liability of members is limited, state that fact clearly on bill heads, notices, letter papers, and outside every office.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: If a foreign company fails to deliver documents under Section 380, what liability do the officers in default face?
options: Only civil damages
Punishable under Section 392 with fine and imprisonment
Only administrative warning by RoC
Immediate deportation of directors
plain.explanation: Section 392 provides that any failure by a foreign company to comply with Chapter XXII makes the company and every officer in default punishable with fine and imprisonment or both as specified under the penal provisions.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Are the provisions of Chapter VI (Registration of Charges) applicable to a foreign company in relation to charges on property situated in India?
options: No, charges of foreign companies are governed entirely by foreign laws
Yes, Section 384 applies the provisions relating to registration of charges to charges created by a foreign company on property in India
Only if approved by the Reserve Bank of India
Yes, but only for floating charges
plain.explanation: Section 384 specifically applies the provisions of Chapter VI (Registration of Charges) to a foreign company as if it were a company incorporated in India, in respect of property situated in India.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the requirement regarding the audit of accounts of a foreign company's Indian business operations?
options: Accounts must be audited by a chartered accountant in practice in India
Accounts can be audited by any auditor qualified in the home country
No audit is required if audited globally
Audit must be conducted exclusively by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
plain.explanation: Section 381(2) requires that the balance sheet and profit and loss account of a foreign company shall be audited by a practicing Chartered Accountant in India, or a firm of chartered accountants.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which form is filed by a foreign company to register its particulars upon establishing a place of business in India under Section 380?
options: Form INC-1
Form FC-1
Form FC-2
Form FC-4
plain.explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014 specifies that an application for registration by a foreign company must be made in Form FC-1 along with necessary attachments.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Does the definition of foreign company under Section 2(42) include an entity operating exclusively through electronic mode?
options: No, electronic mode business is exempt from company law regulations
Yes, provided it conducts business activity in India through electronic mode
Only if it maintains a physical warehouse in India
Only if turnover exceeds 100 crores INR
plain.explanation: Section 2(42) explicitly includes companies incorporated outside India that have a place of business in India 'whether by itself or through an agent, physically or through electronic mode', expanding the scope to e-commerce and digital platforms.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Within what period must a foreign company file particulars of any alteration in its directors or secretary with the RoC?
options: 15 days
30 days
60 days
90 days
plain.explanation: Under Section 380(3), any alteration in the documents filed initially, including changes in directors or secretary, must be filed with the RoC within 30 days of the alteration.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: If a foreign company ceases to have a place of business in India, what is its obligation regarding notice to the RoC?
options: It can simply abandon operations without notice
It must forthwith give notice to the Registrar, and from the date of such notice, its obligation to file ceases
It must wait for 5 years before giving notice
Notice must be published in international newspapers only
plain.explanation: Under the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014, when a foreign company ceases to have a place of business in India, it shall forthwith give notice to the Registrar, and thereafter the obligation of the company to deliver any document to the Registrar ceases.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following is considered part of 'electronic mode' under Rule 3?
options: B2B and B2C web-based transactions
Offline telephonic conversations
Physical courier shipments
Postal mail correspondence
plain.explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014 defines electronic mode to include business-to-business and business-to-consumer transactions, data interchange, and other digital business services.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Who must sign the annual financial statement and return filed by a foreign company in India?
options: Only the home country auditor
Authorized representative of the foreign company in India
The Prime Minister of the home country
Any random employee in India
plain.explanation: The financial statements and annual returns filed by a foreign company under Section 381 must be authenticated by the authorized representative of the foreign company in India.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Can a foreign company accept deposits in India under the provisions of Chapter XXII read with RBI guidelines?
options: Yes, freely from the general public
No foreign company can accept or renew deposits in India unless in compliance with RBI regulations and applicable company law deposit rules
Yes, without any restriction
Only if incorporated in Mauritius
plain.explanation: Acceptance of deposits by foreign companies in India is strictly regulated and restricted, requiring compliance with RBI regulations and provisions applicable to deposit acceptance.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What documents must be attached when a foreign company files Form FC-1 for establishing a place of business?
options: Charter, statutes, or memorandum and articles translated into English
Personal tax returns of all shareholders
Land title deeds of properties in home country
Passports of all global customers
plain.explanation: Form FC-1 must be accompanied by certified translated copies of the charter, statutes, or memorandum and articles of association of the foreign company if they are not in English.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 deals specifically with the accounts of foreign companies?
options: Section 128
Section 381
Section 390
Section 379
plain.explanation: Section 381 of the Companies Act, 2013 contains specific provisions regarding the accounts of a foreign company, requiring maintenance of books of account in India and annual financial statement filing.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: If a foreign company fails to pay the fine imposed under Section 392, who can be held liable among its officers?
options: Only the external auditors
Every officer in default who is in default of compliance
No one, the liability is extinguished
Only shareholders holding more than 50% shares
plain.explanation: Section 392 penalizes 'every officer of the foreign company who is in default', subjecting them to fines and imprisonment as stipulated under the Act.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 386, what is the meaning of 'certified copy' when required for documents delivered to the RoC by a foreign company?
options: Certified in the manner prescribed for documents originating in the home country as a true copy
Certified by any Indian citizen living abroad
Self-attested by a company clerk
Certified by local police
plain.explanation: Section 386 defines 'certified copy' as a copy certified in the manner prescribed by rules, typically certified as a true copy in the country of incorporation in accordance with local laws and notarized/apostilled.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Are Indian companies laws regarding corporate social responsibility (CSR) automatically applicable to foreign companies having a branch in India?
options: Yes, all foreign branches must spend 2% of global profits on CSR
Applicability is determined based on the net worth, turnover, or net profit thresholds of the Indian business operations of the foreign company as per Section 135
No, CSR does not apply to foreign companies at all
Only if explicitly ordered by the Supreme Court
plain.explanation: CSR provisions under Section 135 apply to foreign companies having a branch office or project office in India, based on the financial thresholds computed for their Indian business operations.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which office of the Registrar of Companies has jurisdiction over all foreign companies registered in India?
options: RoC Mumbai
RoC Delhi
RoC Chennai
RoC Kolkata
plain.explanation: By notification and administrative allocation under the Companies Act, the Registrar of Companies at Delhi (RoC Delhi) has centralized jurisdiction for registration and filing of documents by all foreign companies in India.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Global Tech Inc., a corporation incorporated in Delaware, USA, establishes a branch office in Bengaluru, India, on 1st April 2026 to provide software consulting services. The company commences its physical operations immediately. Mr. Smith is appointed as the authorized representative in India. The company delivers its charter, list of directors, and address details to RoC Delhi on 25th May 2026.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Did Global Tech Inc. comply with the initial document delivery timeline under Section 380?
options: Yes, because documents were delivered within 60 days
No, because documents must be delivered within 30 days of establishing a place of business
Yes, because foreign companies get 90 days grace period
No, because filing must be done before commencing business
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 380 requires a foreign company to deliver documents within 30 days of establishing a place of business. Global Tech Inc. established its place on 1st April and filed on 25th May (54 days later), thereby missing the 30-day statutory timeline.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: To which Registrar of Companies should Global Tech Inc. have delivered its registration documents?
options: RoC Bengaluru
RoC Mumbai
RoC Delhi
RoC Delaware
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per administrative jurisdiction under the Companies Act, 2013, all foreign companies register and file their initial incorporation documents with the Registrar of Companies, Delhi, regardless of where their Indian branch is physically located.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Global Tech Inc. later appoints a new director in Delaware on 1st July 2026, within what timeframe must it file the return of alteration with the RoC?
options: 15 days
30 days
60 days
90 days
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 380(3) stipulates that any alteration in the documents delivered to the Registrar (including change in directors) must be filed by submitting a return within 30 days of such alteration.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the consequence of Global Tech Inc. failing to file its initial documents within the prescribed 30-day window?
options: Automatic confiscation of Bengaluru office property
Penalty under Section 392 on the company and every officer in default
Revocation of Delaware incorporation
Mandatory imprisonment of all US shareholders
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 392 prescribes penal consequences including fines ranging from ₹1,00,000 to ₹3,00,000 and continuing daily fines for non-compliance with Section 380 by the company and officers in default.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Nippon Auto Ltd., a company incorporated in Japan, operates an online e-commerce platform targeting Indian consumers without having any physical warehouses or offices in India. All transactions, digital contracts, and product deliveries are handled through electronic mode. Nippon Auto Ltd. generates significant revenue from Indian territory during the financial year 2025-26.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Nippon Auto Ltd. classified as a 'foreign company' under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: No, because it lacks a physical office or brick-and-mortar store in India
Yes, because Section 2(42) includes companies incorporated outside India conducting business in India through electronic mode
No, foreign e-commerce is regulated exclusively by IT Act
Yes, but only if it registers a subsidiary in India
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 2(42) explicitly includes companies incorporated outside India that conduct business in India through electronic mode, even without a physical office, within the definition of a foreign company.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which rules define the scope of 'electronic mode' applicable to Nippon Auto Ltd.?
options: Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014
Information Technology Rules, 2021
Foreign Exchange Management Rules, 2016
SEBI Listing Regulations, 2015
linkedMcqs.explanation: Rule 3 of the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules, 2014 defines electronic mode for foreign companies operating in India.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Does Nippon Auto Ltd. need to comply with annual financial statement filing requirements under Section 381?
options: No, electronic mode businesses are exempt from accounting filings
Yes, every foreign company must prepare and file financial statements relating to Indian business operations
Only if turnover exceeds USD 10 million in Japan
Only if directed by the Supreme Court
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 381 applies to all foreign companies, which includes those operating via electronic mode, requiring them to file financial statements and a list of places of business with the RoC annually.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Who must audit the financial statements prepared for Nippon Auto Ltd.'s Indian business operations?
options: Any auditor in Japan
A Chartered Accountant in practice in India
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Internal auditor of the parent company
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 381(2) mandates that the financial statements of a foreign company's Indian business must be audited by a practicing Chartered Accountant in India or a firm of chartered accountants.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: EuroRetail AG, incorporated in Germany, sets up a retail liaison office in Mumbai. The company creates a charge over its machinery situated in Mumbai in favor of an Indian bank. EuroRetail AG fails to register this charge with the RoC within the stipulated time under the Companies Act, 2013.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Are the provisions regarding registration of charges applicable to EuroRetail AG?
options: No, foreign companies are exempt from charge registration
Yes, Section 384 applies Chapter VI provisions to charges created by foreign companies on property situated in India
Only if the charge exceeds ₹100 crores
Yes, but registration must be done in Germany only
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 384 explicitly applies Chapter VI (Registration of Charges) to foreign companies in respect of property situated in India as if they were Indian companies.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Within what period must a charge on property in India be registered by EuroRetail AG?
options: 10 days
30 days
60 days
90 days
linkedMcqs.explanation: Charges created by a company (including a foreign company under Section 384) on property in India must be registered within 30 days of creation, extendable with approval.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the legal consequence of failing to register the charge created by EuroRetail AG?
options: The charge becomes void against the liquidator and any creditor of the company
The German directors are imprisoned immediately
The machinery is auctioned by RBI
The loan agreement becomes illegal
linkedMcqs.explanation: Non-registration of a charge under Chapter VI (applied via Section 384) renders the charge void against the liquidator and any creditor of the company.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Where must EuroRetail AG maintain its books of account regarding its Indian operations?
options: Exclusively in Frankfurt, Germany
At its principal place of business in India
At the Reserve Bank of India headquarters
At the Ministry of Corporate Affairs office in Delhi
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 381(1) requires a foreign company to keep at its principal place of business in India proper books of account with respect to monies received/expended, sales/purchases, and assets/liabilities of the Indian business.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Pacific Holdings Ltd., incorporated in Singapore, establishes a place of business in Chennai. The company displays its name outside its Chennai office only in English. It omits mentioning its country of incorporation and whether its members' liability is limited on its business letterheads used in India.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Did Pacific Holdings Ltd. comply with Section 382 regarding name display outside its office?
options: Yes, English is sufficient
No, it must exhibit its name and country of incorporation in English and in the local language of the place where its office is situated
Yes, if approved by RoC Delhi
No, it must display only in Tamil
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 382 mandates that every foreign company shall paint or affix its name and the country of incorporation outside every office in English and in the local language of the place.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the requirement regarding business letterheads under Section 382 for Pacific Holdings Ltd.?
options: It must state the company name, country of incorporation, and whether liability of members is limited
It must state the PAN and GSTIN only
It must state the home country stock exchange ticker
No particulars are required on letterheads
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 382 requires that business letter heads, bill heads, and notices must state the name of the foreign company, country of incorporation, and whether the liability of members is limited.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Pacific Holdings Ltd. decides to close down its Chennai place of business, what procedure must it follow?
options: Abandon premises without informing anyone
Give notice forthwith to the Registrar of Companies, after which filing obligations cease
Wait 3 years before notifying RoC
File a winding-up petition in Singapore High Court
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the rules framed for foreign companies, when a foreign company ceases to have a place of business in India, it must forthwith give notice to the Registrar, upon which its obligation to deliver documents ceases.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What penalty can be imposed for non-compliance with the name display and letterhead requirements under Section 382?
options: Fine under Section 392 ranging between ₹1,00,000 and ₹3,00,000 with continuing daily fine
Warning letter only
Immediate forfeiture of office furniture
Deportation of local employees
linkedMcqs.explanation: General penalty provision under Section 392 applies to any contravention of Chapter XXII, which includes failure to comply with Section 382 name display and letterhead rules.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Alpha Corp, a company incorporated in the UK, decides to issue a prospectus in India offering shares to the Indian public. Alpha Corp delivers a copy of the prospectus to RoC Delhi. However, the prospectus fails to state the specific details of the instruments and material contracts required under Section 390 read with Section 389.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: To which RoC must Alpha Corp deliver its prospectus prior to issue in India?
options: RoC London
RoC Mumbai
RoC Delhi
RoC Kolkata
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 389 specifies that a copy of the prospectus must be delivered to the Registrar of Companies (specifically RoC Delhi) before it is issued, circulated, or distributed in India.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is a mandatory prerequisite for issuing a prospectus by a foreign company in India?
options: Consent of SEBI alone
Delivery of a copy of the prospectus to the RoC signed by all directors or their authorized agents
Approval from British High Commission
Listing on London Stock Exchange
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 389 requires that no prospectus shall be issued unless a copy thereof has been delivered to the Registrar, signed by every director or his agent authorized in writing.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Alpha Corp issues a defective prospectus in India, what liability do persons authorizing the issue face?
options: Only contractual liability in the UK
Criminal liability for misstatement in prospectus under Section 447 and general penal provisions
No liability in India
Civil damages limited to ₹10,000
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 390 makes provisions relating to prospectus applicable to foreign companies, and misstatements or omissions attract penal consequences including criminal liability under Section 447 and general penalty provisions.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Must the prospectus issued by Alpha Corp specify the date and incorporate details of material contracts?
options: No, foreign prospectuses are exempt from material contract disclosures
Yes, Section 390/391 mandates disclosures similar to domestic prospectuses including material contracts and consents
Only if shares exceed 50% of capital
Only at the discretion of the UK directors
linkedMcqs.explanation: Sections 390 and 391 prescribe detailed disclosures to be contained in a foreign company's prospectus, including particulars of contracts, time and place of inspection, and expert consents.
